plan_a_advantages: More targeted hill work for trail-specific power development.
Includes strength training to improve running power and resilience.
More varied workout types (hills, long runs, easy runs) provide a broader stimulus.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses primarily on building a strong aerobic base, which is a foundational element for any runner.
Longer, steady-state runs can contribute to overall endurance and comfort on trails.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted hill work and shorter, more intense interval sessions (hill repeats) which directly address improving running power and efficiency on varied terrain – crucial for trail running. Plan B focuses almost entirely on aerobic endurance with longer, steady-state runs, which, while beneficial, doesn't provide the same stimulus for speed development. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training further supports the goal of increased power and resilience, while Plan B’s lack of this element is a significant omission.
